The intelligent man, when blessing comes upon him and the world turns toward him with what he loves of its matters — let him humble himself, out of fear that it be a vengeance from God upon him, as the Wise One said: "Wealth kept by its owner to his harm" (Ecclesiastes 5:12).

**The sixth**: when he reads the Book of God and the books of the prophets, with their promise and their threat, and recognizes from himself a falling-short in the rights of God and of the people of his time — humility and self-lowering before God (exalted be He) are incumbent upon him out of fear of His punishment, as He said of Josiah (peace be upon him): "And it was, when the king heard the words of the Book of the Law, that he tore his garments" (2 Kings 22:11); and God said to him: "Because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before the Lord when you heard what I had spoken about this place and against its dwellers, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and you tore your garments and wept before Me — even I have heard, says the Lord" (2 Kings 22:19).

**The seventh**: when he undertakes the doing of any of the works of obedience to God — like prayer, charity, a Law-precept, a supererogatory act, or an admonition — let him not undertake that with anything in his heart of conceit or pride; rather let him humble himself and abase himself before God in his outer and his inner. Let his measure not be great in his own sight in the face of the magnitude of what is binding upon him toward God in the like of that work, as He said: "With what shall I come before the Lord? With what shall I bow myself before the high God? Will the Lord be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil?" — He said: "He has told you, O man, what is good, and what does the Lord seek of you but to do justice and to love kindness and to walk humbly with your God?" (Micah 6:6, 8).
